text.p: VIENNA July 11 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Friday are:

- Two big shareholders of insurance company Bundeslaender will contest the company's decision to pay preference shareholders an unchanged dividend of 12 schillings but to pay nothing out to ordinary shareholders.

- The Social Democrats and conservative People's Party lock horns over the issue of lowering the alcohol limit for drivers from 0.8 promille to 0.5. Conservatives say they were bullied by the Social Democrats to reject the lower limit.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said his budget deficit plans remain steadfast.
- Austria's largest paper maker Frantschach said it is in "exclusive talks" with the Polish government over buying Poland's largest paper maker. It expects to get the go-ahead this year.
- Casinos Austria turns in another record year of profits in 1996. Shareholders will be paid a 12 schilling dividend.

- With friction palpable in the coalition government after the alcohol limit vote, observers are keen to see how the dominant Social Democrats will react to the opposition parties' votes of no-confidence in conservative People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel in parliament today.

- Economic research institute WIFO will revise downwards its forecast for the country's current account following a huge widening in the deficit in the period from January to May. WIFO had been looking for an improvement in the deficit for 1997 of 39 billion schillings. WIFO now thinks it will about match last year's deficit of 42.4 billion schillings.
- Kangaroo meat was the most favourite exotic meat in Austria's restaurants last year.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische expands its Easter European base by taking over a majority stake in the Kooperativa insurance group, which is active in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
- Finance Minister Edlinger says he does not plan changing the country's banking secrecy laws despite pressure from the EU.
